title: Bibliometric Analysis of Global Research Trends on Probiotic-Based Interventions for Postmenopausal Osteoporosis.
abstract: Postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP) is a major skeletal disorder associated with increased fracture risk and substantial morbidity. Growing evidence links the gut microbiota with bone homeostasis, supporting investigation of probiotic-based interventions through immunomodulation, maintenance of intestinal barrier function, and production of short-chain fatty acids. Existing bibliometric studies have examined broader relationships between the gut microbiota, bone metabolism, and osteoporosis; the ...

title: Early post-weaning probiotic supplementation alters gut microbial community structure and predicted metabolic function in female juvenile mice.
abstract: To characterize the effects of early post-weaning multi-strain probiotic supplementation on gut microbiota composition, predicted metabolic function, and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) profiles in female juvenile mice at the pubertal window.

title: Targeting the gut-tumor axis: probiotic therapy as an adjunct strategy in colorectal cancer treatment.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a multifactorial disease driven by interactions among host genetics, immune dysregulation, environmental factors, and gut microbiota. The gut-tumor axis regulates CRC progression through inflammatory signaling, oxidative stress, epithelial barrier disruption, and immune imbalance. Probiotic-derived metabolites act as bioactive molecules capable of restoring host-microbiome homeostasis and modulating tumor-associated pathways.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

title: Macronutrient-based interventions and TB treatment outcomes: a scoping review.
abstract: <sec><title>INTRODUCTION</title>Macronutrients may influence TB outcomes through biological and clinical mechanisms. We conducted a scoping review to map evidence on macronutrient-based nutritional interventions during TB treatment and their associations with treatment outcomes and clinical recovery.</sec><sec><title>METHODS</title>Following Joanna Briggs Institute guidelines, a protocol was prospectively registered. We systematically searched MEDLINE, Embase, Global Health, Food Science and Tec...
journal: The international journal of tuberculosis and lung disease : the official journal of the International Union against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease

title: Clinical effects of multi-strain probiotics in extremely preterm infants: a multicenter pre-post implementation study in the Netherlands.
abstract: Probiotics may reduce the risk of necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), late-onset sepsis (LOS), and mortality in preterm infants. However, their efficacy in extremely preterm infants (gestational age < 28 weeks) is still regularly questioned due to limited data and safety concerns. In Dutch Neonatal Intensive Care Units (NICUs), a three-strain probiotic product (ProPrems®; Bifidobacterium infantis Bb-02, Bifidobacterium lactis BB-12, and Streptococcus thermophilus TH-4) was implemented as standard o...

title: Therapeutic Role of Probiotics in Regulating Mental Health: Gut-Brain Cross-Talk.
abstract: The gastrointestinal tract harbors a diverse microbial community, including bacteria, archaea, and protozoa, which play pivotal roles in maintaining host gut health. Probiotics, comprising nonpathogenic microorganisms administered in appropriate doses, have garnered attention for their therapeutic potential in promoting overall human health. They bolster antipathogenic defenses, enhance immune function, and ameliorate gastrointestinal disorders like irritable bowel syndrome. The intricate interp...
journal: Journal of environmental pathology, toxicology and oncology : official organ of the International Society for Environmental Toxicology and Cancer

title: Super-resolution mapping of nuclear stress signaling by probiotic-derived extracellular vesicles in UV-induced skin photodamage.
abstract: Ultraviolet (UV)-induced photodamage drives oxidative stress, DNA damage, and chronic inflammation, leading to progressive cellular ultrastructure and skin function degeneration. Despite the potential of probiotics as anti-photodamage agents, their nanoscale action mechanism remains unexplored. title: Effect of probiotic root canal irrigation on macrophage polarization in rat periapical lesions.
abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of the probiotic Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis HN019 as a root canal irrigant on the polarization of macrophages into M1 and M2 subtypes in periapical lesions induced in rats, using immunohistochemical analysis. Forty-eight adult male Wistar Hannover rats were divided into six groups: Group I (4 animals/8 teeth): sound teeth; Group II (4 animals/4 teeth): 2.5% sodium hypochlorite as the irrigation solution (3 days); Group III (4 animals/4...

title: The effect of micronutrient supplementation on women's sexual desire: a systematic review and meta-analysis study.
abstract: The aim of this study was to determine the effectiveness of micronutrient supplementation on female sexual desire levels.

title: Microbiome-Immune Crosstalk in Inflammatory Skin Diseases: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential of Probiotics.
abstract: The gut-skin axis links intestinal microbial activity with inflammatory skin disease, yet findings across atopic dermatitis, acne vulgaris, and psoriasis remain inconsistent. This review examines how disease biology and host context shape microbiome-related effects and responses to probiotics.

title: Bletilla striata-derived extracellular vesicles armed probiotic by supramolecular assembly ameliorates colitis via macrophage modulation and microbiota restoration.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) represents major global health challenges, but current treatments often are limited by efficacy loss, infection risks, and disruption of gut homeostasis. Novel therapies are needed to actively promote mucosal repair and restore immune balance.

title: Effects of selenium supplementation on glycemic indices and oxidative-stress biomarkers in adults: a systematic review, meta-analysis, and dose-response analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: Diabetes and metabolic syndrome are major public health challenges closely linked to oxidative stress, inflammation, and impaired insulin signaling. Selenium, an essential trace element with antioxidant and immunomodulatory roles, has been proposed as an adjunctive strategy for metabolic regulation; however, evidence from randomized trials remains inconsistent. We evaluated the effects of selenium supplementation on glycemic indices, oxidative-stress-related biomarkers, lipid metabolism, and rel...

title: Effects of Beauveria bassiana Alone and Combined with Yeast-Fermented Prebiotics on Hypothenemus hampei.
abstract: The coffee berry borer (CBB) Hypothenemus hampei is the major pest of coffee crops worldwide. The use of prebiotics may help increase the efficiency of Beauveria bassiana biological control by enhancing CBB attractiveness or providing a nutritive substrate that may enable the entomopathogenic fungus to initiate the infection process more rapidly. This study evaluated whether the application of B. bassiana combined with yeast-fermented prebiotics affects the attractiveness, development, and infes...

title: Is plant-based protein supplementation as effective as whey protein? A systematic review and meta-analysis in untrained adults undergoing resistance training.
abstract: Dietary protein supplements are commonly consumed to support increases in lean body mass among healthy adults engaged in resistance training (RT). Although whey protein has been extensively investigated, plant-based protein supplements have emerged as a viable alternative for individuals who avoid animal-derived products.
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

title: Effects of Oral Resveratrol Supplementation on Inflammatory and Cardiometabolic Outcomes in Adults: Protocol for a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Resveratrol is a naturally occurring polyphenol found primarily in grapes, berries, peanuts, and red wine. Experimental evidence suggests that resveratrol modulates multiple biological pathways involved in oxidative stress, inflammation, insulin signaling, endothelial function, and metabolic homeostasis. However, findings from randomized controlled trials remain inconsistent, and previous evidence syntheses have reported substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity.

title: Gut-Mammary Axis-Mediated Improvement of Sialylated Milk Oligosaccharide Synthesis by Polygonatum sibiricum Polysaccharide and Probiotics in Mice with Gestational Metabolic Disorders.
abstract: Milk oligosaccharides (MOs) are vital for infant health but vulnerable to gestational metabolic dysfunction. To explore a new microecological intervention strategy, we established a probiotic fermentation platform coupled with a mammary epithelial cell screening model to identify Polygonatum sibiricum polysaccharide (PSP) as a promising candidate. Murine models demonstrated that both PSP monotherapy and synergistic treatment with probiotics significantly mitigated gestational metabolic dysregula...
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: [Effect of postoperative nutritional supplementation on the reduction of clinical complications in geriatric patients with hip fracture: a retrospective study in a hospital setting].
abstract: The high incidence of hip fractures among the elderly population in Spain, with an estimated 50,000 to 60,000 cases annually, represents a serious public health issue due to high mortality rates and associated complications, particularly in malnourished patients. The objective of this paper was to assess the effectiveness of nutritional supplementation as part of postoperative treatment in elderly patients with hip fractures.

title: Investigating the Effect of Oral Probiotic Capsules on Postpartum Sleep Quality in Primiparous Women: A triple-blind randomised controlled trial.
abstract: Quality of sleep is an important indicator of health. Sleep disturbance and daytime fatigue is one of the most common problems in the postpartum period. Early postpartum (first 4 weeks) is when sleep is most disturbed. The gut microbiota may affect sleep quality and affect host health through the production of metabolites and compounds. This study aimed to determine the effect of oral probiotic capsule on the quality of sleep after delivery in primiparous women.

title: Antioxidants in male infertility: from empirical supplementation to phenotype directed therapy.
abstract: Oxidative stress is a biologically plausible contributor to male infertility, and antioxidant supplementation has been investigated for decades. Yet clinical evidence has not converged on a reproducible benefit in reproductive outcomes. The 2025 World Health Organization (WHO) infertility guideline made no recommendation for or against antioxidant supplementation in men with infertility and one or more semen parameters outside WHO reference ranges, reflecting uncertainty rather than proof of uni...

title: Preventive administration of Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis HEM20-01 attenuates the development of atopic dermatitis-like inflammation in mice, along with gut microbial and succinate alterations.
abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder frequently accompanied by gut dysbiosis and neurobehavioral comorbidities, but the microbial metabolites mediating gut-skin crosstalk remain unclear. We investigated whether preventive administration of Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis HEM20-01 attenuates the development of AD-like phenotypes and characterized the accompanying gut microbiome, succinate, intestinal, and behavioral alterations.

title: The effect of four types of iron supplements on enamel microhardness of primary teeth: an in-vitro study.
abstract: Iron supplementation has been suggested as a potential factor influencing enamel properties; however, its direct effect on enamel microhardness remains unclear. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of four types of supplements on the microhardness of deciduous tooth enamel.

title: The effects of oral magnesium supplements on vascular and endothelial function: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: Magnesium has been suggested to play a role in cardiovascular health through its effects on endothelial function, vascular stiffness, and blood pressure. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to update and evaluate the effect of magnesium supplementation on vascular function and cardiometabolic outcomes in adults.

title: Maternal Supplementation With Rumen-Protected Methionine and Trace Minerals During Lactation Improves Growth Performance and Increases the Abundance of Fiber-Degrading Bacteria in Yak Calves.
abstract: This study was conducted to investigate the effects of trace minerals (TM) and rumen-protected methionine (RPM) maternal supplementation on growth performance and rumen bacteria in yak calves. Six 3-month-old yak calves (bodyweight: 38.5 ± 3 kg) were selected from each maternal diet group (control [CON], TM, and RPM group) and named as follows: CON-YC (CON group yak calves), TM-YC (TM group yak calves), and RPM-YC (RPM group yak calves). title: Physicochemical and Sensory Properties of Probiotic Fermented Sheep Milk Fortified with Inulin and Sodium Butyrate.
abstract: Background/Objectives: In the production of functional foods, bioactive compounds are commonly incorporated into the product, including dietary fibre, polyols, probiotics and prebiotics, unsaturated fatty acids, vitamins, minerals, and other health-promoting constituents. Such ingredients are used, among others, for the fortification of dairy products. title: Maternal DHA Supplementation and Fetal Brain Development: Benefits, Risks, and Individual Needs.
abstract: Maternal nutrition is a key determinant of fetal development, particularly in the context of neural regulation and maturation. Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids, especially docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), play an essential role in neural differentiation, synaptogenesis, myelination, and neuroprotection. While the neurodevelopmental benefits of DHA are well-documented, the effects of excessive maternal DHA intake and the potential long-term consequences on offspring neurophysiology remain poorly un...

title: Dietary Patterns and Nutritional Interventions for Cognitive Impairment in Parkinson's Disease: A Critical Narrative Review.
abstract: Cognitive impairment affects most people with Parkinson's disease (PD); mild cognitive impairment is present in 25-40% of people with PD without dementia, and nutritional advice often exceeds the evidence. We reviewed the human evidence that dietary patterns or nutritional supplements improve cognition in established PD, separating objective cognitive outcomes from patient-rated and biomarker outcomes.

title: Effects of Caffeine-Taurine Co-Supplementation on Exercise Performance: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background: Caffeine-taurine combinations are widely used in commercial sports products. Whether this combination improves exercise performance is still unclear. This study aimed to estimate the effect of caffeine-taurine co-supplementation versus placebo on exercise performance. Methods: Randomized controlled trials comparing caffeine plus taurine versus placebo were searched in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and related databases up to June 1, 2026. title: Melatonin and Female Fertility: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical Supplementation, In Vitro Experiments, and Observational Evidence.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Melatonin has been proposed as a potential strategy to improve female fertility, but existing evidence is dispersed across assisted reproduction, reproductive disorders, and in vitro studies. This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the relationships of melatonin supplementation, in vitro melatonin treatment, and endogenous melatonin levels with female fertility. Methods: PubMed, Web of Science, and EMBASE were searched from inception through February 2026. Randomized ...

title: Effects of Acute Ecklonia cava Supplementation on Submaximal Cycling and Repeated-Sprint Performance in Trained Cyclists: A Randomised Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled Crossover Trial.
abstract: This study examined whether acute Ecklonia cava (EC) ingestion altered physiological responses during submaximal cycling or power output during subsequent repeated maximal sprints in experienced male cyclists.

title: Food-Grade Metal-Phenolic Network and Polysaccharide Microencapsulation Enhances the In Vivo Anti-Colitic Efficacy of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum B112.
abstract: Probiotic therapy for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) has a persistent practical obstacle: most cells given by mouth die before they reach the colon.

title: Impact of Probiotic Intervention on Lymphocyte Activity in Mice Challenged with Pea Albumins (Pisum sativum L.).
abstract: Background: Probiotics are microorganisms with proven health benefits in humans. However, the mechanisms underlying the direct effects of these compounds on immune cells remain unclear. This study aimed to examine the effects of probiotics on immunity in mice exposed to allergenic dietary proteins, specifically pea albumin (PA). title: Effects of Chondroitin Sulfate on Joint Symptoms and Physical Function in Adults with Mild Knee Osteoarthritis: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Although chondroitin sulfate (CS) is commonly used for knee osteoarthritis (OA), evidence regarding its effects on joint symptoms and physical function remains inconsistent. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of CS supplementation on joint symptoms and physical function in adults with mild knee OA. title: Consumption of Energy Drinks and Use of Dietary Supplements Among Italian University Students: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: The rising consumption of energy drinks (ED) and dietary supplements (DS) among youth raises public health concerns, particularly regarding uncontrolled use, excessive dosages, and product combinations. This study assessed ED and DS use among a sample of university students in Southern Italy and identified associations with sociodemographic and lifestyle characteristics.

title: Immunonutrition vs. Standard Oral Nutritional Supplements in Prehabilitation for Colorectal Cancer Surgery: A Randomized Clinical Trial Assessing Morbidity and Body Composition by Computed Tomography.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Perioperative immunonutrition (IMN) has been proposed to improve outcomes after colorectal surgery. However, the evidence is heterogeneous, and few studies have assessed morbidity together with computed tomography (CT)-derived body composition. We compared IMN with standard oral nutritional supplementation (SONS) in patients undergoing colorectal cancer surgery, evaluating postoperative complications and changes in body composition. title: Effects of a Saccharomyces uvarum Cell-Based Preparation on Gut Microbial Ecology and Metabolic Activity in Adults Without Diagnosed Gastrointestinal Disease: A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Crossover Pilot Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Yeast-based probiotic candidates are increasingly investigated as potential modulators of gut ecology, although evidence in healthy individuals remains limited. This randomized, single-blind, crossover study primarily evaluated the tolerability of ATECREM Serius containing Saccharomyces uvarum SERIUS strain (>1010 CFU/g) and explored its effect on human gut microbiota. title: Comparative Effectiveness of Nutritional Strategies for Sarcopenia-Related Outcomes in Older Adults: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Objective: This study compared the relative effects of distinct nutritional strategies on muscle mass, muscle strength, and physical performance in older adults with sarcopenia or at high risk of sarcopenia. Methods: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and CNKI were systematically searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs). title: Effects of Yeast Protein-Whey Protein Composite Supplementation on Recovery from Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage in Well-Trained Athletes: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Objectives: Exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD) can impair muscle function and subsequent athletic performance. This study examined whether an isonitrogenous yeast protein-whey protein composite (YP) modifies recovery from EIMD compared with whey protein (WP) and a water-only control (C) in well-trained athletes. title: Nutraceutical Periodization for eXercise (NPX): Matching Bioactives to Training Load, Recovery Demand, and Adaptation Windows.
abstract: Nutraceuticals are evaluated as though efficacy were a stable ingredient property, although net value may vary with exercise stimulus, exposure schedule, recovery pressure, athlete state, and prioritized outcome. This structured narrative review integrates exercise-adaptation biology, periodized sports nutrition, training-load and recovery models, precision nutrition, and human evidence for sport-relevant interventions. title: Dietary Polyphenols as Adjunctive Therapy for Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract: Dietary polyphenols have been studied as adjunctive therapies for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), but trials vary in formulation, clinical setting, and outcome definitions. We evaluated efficacy and safety separately for ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn's disease (CD).

title: Folic Acid Supplementation Adherence During Pregnancy: Evidence from a Cross-Sectional Survey in Italy.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Periconceptional folic acid (FA) supplementation is a cornerstone of primary prevention of neural tube defects (NTDs). However, adequate preconceptional FA intake remains suboptimal in Italy. This study aimed to assess FA use among pregnant women in the Calabria region, determine whether their intake met United States Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) recommendations, and explore potential predictors that shape these practices. title: Effectiveness of Supplemental Feeding Combined with Nutrition Education on Child Nutrition Outcomes in Kenya.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Nutrition education coupled with supplemental feeding has been shown to be an effective intervention to combat child undernutrition. However, evidence of such interventions remains scarce in pastoralist communities in Kenya despite a high burden of child undernutrition. title: Limosilactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938 Attenuates Hyperoxia-Induced Lung Injury in a Newborn Rat Model.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) remains a leading cause of morbidity in preterm infants, and effective preventive strategies are lacking. This study investigated the protective effect of orally administered Limosilactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938 in a neonatal rat model of hyperoxia-induced lung injury. title: New Vitamin and Mineral Supplements: Acceptability, Tolerability, and Short-Term Adherence in a Paediatric Cohort with IMDs.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Dietary therapy for inherited metabolic disorders (IMDs) can restrict nutrient-dense foods and increase reliance on vitamin and mineral supplementation. However, formulation-related barriers may limit supplement acceptability and adherence, particularly in children with feeding difficulties and complex dietary regimens. title: Lactobacillus rhamnosus Lysate for Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Background and Objectives: Modulation of the gut-liver axis with non-viable microbial components is a promising approach to correct metabolic disorders. The aim of the study was to evaluate the short-term efficacy and safety of the postbiotic lysate Lactobacillus rhamnosus DV-NRRL B-68023 on non-invasive measures of hepatic steatosis, transaminase activity, and anthropometric parameters in patients with MASLD. title: Source-Dependent Renal Effects of Commercial Protein Supplements: A 28-Day Study in Rats.
abstract: Background and Objectives: Commercial protein powders are widely consumed to increase dietary protein intake, yet whether their renal effects differ by protein source remains poorly characterized. The primary objective of this study was therefore to determine whether 28 days of administration of commercial whey, casein, soy or beef protein powder produces source-dependent renal histopathological injury in rats, with the total renal injury score as the primary outcome. abstract: Gastrointestinal infections remain a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Conventional antibiotic treatment can be ineffective or inappropriate in some settings, particularly in the context of increasing antimicrobial resistance. title: Profiling of Bioactive Metabolites and In Vitro Multifunctional Properties of Postbiotic Cell-Free Supernatant Derived from Probiotic Lactic Acid Bacteria Isolated from Fermented Olives.
abstract: This work aims to characterize the bioactive metabolite profile and in vitro multifunctional properties of postbiotic cell-free supernatants (Postbiotic-CFSs) derived from three lactic acid bacteria (Levilactobacillus brevis S27, Lactiplantibacillus pentosus S42, and Lactiplantibacillus plantarum S62) isolated from fermented green olives. title: The Screening and Identification of Potential Probiotics in Misgurnus anguillicaudatus Intestine.
abstract: We characterized the intestinal microbiota of Misgurnus anguillicaudatus using 16S rRNA gene sequencing (V4 region). Strains secreting extracellular digestive enzymes were functionally screened, identified by 16S rRNA sequencing, and evaluated for biosafety. Microbial diversity analysis revealed that the intestinal microbiota of M. anguillicaudatus was dominated by the genera Vibrio, Pseudoalteromonas, and Aeromonas as core predominant taxa. title: Chronic Ultrasound ('Emotional') Stress in Mice Exacerbates Colitis Through GSK3β-Mediated Neuroimmune Dysregulation and Is Ameliorated by Probiotic Intervention.
abstract: Background: Growing evidence supports a bidirectional relationship between 'emotional' (psychological) stress and intestinal inflammation. 'Emotional stress', a form of stress that is triggered by negative information and experiences of non-physical nature, is an established risk factor for the development of subclinical intestinal inflammation, called irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), to inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). title: Methylsulfonylmethane as a Bioactive Nutraceutical: Molecular Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence, Combination Therapy, Dosing, and Safety.
abstract: Methylsulfonylmethane (MSM; dimethyl sulfone) is an organosulfur nutraceutical used primarily for joint symptoms, although its molecular actions and clinical applicability beyond osteoarthritis remain uncertain. This narrative review integrates pharmacological, preclinical, and human evidence on MSM, with emphasis on musculoskeletal disorders, multi-ingredient formulations, dosing, safety, toxicology, and clinical monitoring.
